meaning: to earn just enough money to pay for basic needs
example: After he lost his job, it was hard for him to make ends meet.
origin: It is believed to come from the idea of stretching a small amount of money so that the two ends of a budget meet

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a race at the same time as someone
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Nothing in the idiom refers to racing or finishing at the same time; it is about money.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to repair two broken things at once
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with repairing objects; it describes a financial situation.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to pay back all your debts at the end of the year
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom describes struggling to cover basic costs, not clearing debts completely.

explanation: 'Make ends meet' describes having just enough money to cover everyday expenses such as food, rent and bills. It is often used when money is tight.
